핵심이슈.summary:
## 오늘의 한국 경제 흐름 요약

국내 증시가 코스피 7,000포인트 시대를 맞이하며 ETF 시장 규모가 440조 원에 육박하는 가운데, 반도체와 레버리지 상품으로의 자금 쏠림이 뚜렷해지고 있다. 이러한 강세장을 배경으로 이재명 대통령은 한국의 순부채비율이 낮다는 IMF 보고서를 직접 공유하며 재정 긴축론에 반박하고, 적극적인 재정 확장의 근거를 제시하는 행보를 보였다. 한편 대외적으로는 EU가 미국의 IRA(인플레이션 감축법)에 맞서는 자국 산업 보호 정책을 강화하면서 배터리·전기차 등 K-산업의 유럽 공급망에 비상이 걸렸다. 결국 오늘의 경제 흐름은 국내 증시 호황과 재정 확대 논의가 맞물리는 가운데, 글로벌 보호무역 장벽이 동시에 높아지는 **기회와 위기가 공존하는 국면**으로 요약된다.

key_headlines.title: President Lee and Finance Minister Gu Counter Austerity Arguments with IMF Data on Low Net Debt Ratio
key_headlines.summary: President Lee and Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yoon-chul refuted claims of fiscal crisis, citing IMF reports showing Korea's net debt ratio is one-eighth that of advanced nations. They emphasized growth-oriented fiscal policy rather than spending cuts.

key_headlines.title: EU Raises Trade Barriers with European IRA, Threatening Korean Supply Chains
key_headlines.summary: The EU is implementing protectionist policies similar to the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act, creating supply chain risks for Korean industries including semiconductors and batteries.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Breaks 7,000 Mark for First Time with Retail Investors and ETFs Leading the Rally
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index surpassed 7,000 for the first time, driven by consistent retail investor buying and concentrated ETF inflows, particularly into semiconductor and leveraged funds totaling 440 trillion won.

key_headlines.title: April Consumer Prices Rise 2.6% in 21 Months Due to Middle East Tensions and Oil Price Surge
key_headlines.summary: April consumer inflation reached 2.6%, the highest in 21 months, as oil prices jumped 22% due to Middle East conflict. The Bank of Korea expects May inflation to widen further with petroleum prices remaining elevated.

key_headlines.title: Jeonse-to-Monthly Rent Conversion Accelerates, with New Apartments Showing 66.7% Monthly Rent Ratio
key_headlines.summary: The rental market shows accelerating conversion of traditional jeonse deposits to monthly rent contracts, with newly built apartment complexes recording 66.7% monthly rent ratios, affecting tenant affordability across the metropolitan area.

sections.Hot Economy News: President Lee and Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yoon-chul confronted austerity advocates by highlighting IMF data showing Korea's net debt ratio is significantly lower than advanced nations, with Q1 GDP growth hitting a 5.5-year high at 5%. The government emphasized growth-oriented fiscal expansion rather than spending restraint as the path to debt sustainability. This positions the administration's active fiscal stance against rising inflation concerns, particularly amid Middle East geopolitical tensions affecting global energy markets.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea reported April consumer prices rose 2.6%, reaching a 21-month high, primarily driven by petroleum prices surging 22% due to Middle East conflict. The central bank forecasts May inflation will widen further as oil prices remain elevated and agricultural price base effects compound the pressure. Expected inflation among the general public rose slightly to 2.9% from 2.7% month-over-month. Government price stabilization measures aim to mitigate upward pressure, though the Bank of Korea flagged Middle East developments and oil price trajectories as key uncertainty factors for future inflation paths.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI index surpassed 7,000 for the first time in history, with intraday trading reaching 7,340 levels, driven by retail investors' consistent buying and concentrated ETF capital flows totaling nearly 440 trillion won, particularly into semiconductor and leveraged funds. The KOSDAQ declined despite KOSPI strength, with biotech and small-cap investors facing losses as memory semiconductor boom drives large-cap gains. Interest rate concerns emerged following hawkish Fed signals, with expectations for potential rate hikes, though currency stability around the 1,500 won-per-dollar level reflects Middle East risk awareness.
sections.Industry & Technology: The OECD warned that even major Korean semiconductor and battery manufacturers face supply chain vulnerabilities in critical materials including cobalt, lithium, nickel, and rare earths. A new Doosan ETF focusing on AI, nuclear power, and robotics surged 39.6% within a month of listing, signaling investor appetite for AI value chain investments. The business community requested regulatory reforms including separate battery sales for electric vehicles and copyright exemptions for AI training data. Japanese Honda indefinitely postponed its Canadian electric vehicle plant construction due to weaker-than-expected North American EV demand.
sections.Real Estate: Housing price appreciation expectations among experts dropped sharply from 81% to 56% over three months following strong government market stabilization policies. The jeonse-to-monthly rent conversion phenomenon accelerates, with newly built apartments showing 66.7% monthly rent ratios and overall Seoul monthly rent share reaching 48.6%, exceeding jeonse transactions in March at 50.1%. Monthly rent concentrations are particularly pronounced in new construction and smaller units, with metropolitan area monthly rent ratios surpassing 70%. Tenant affordability pressures mount as monthly rent becomes increasingly dominant across the rental market.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Federal Reserve maintained interest rates in its final FOMC meeting under Chair Powell, citing persistent inflation concerns despite solid growth, though three voting members advocated for rate hikes. President Trump mocked Fed Chair Powell over interest rate levels, demanding reductions. Global inflation risks resurged from Middle East tensions and rising energy prices, with the Australian central bank conducting its third rate hike of 2026, signaling potential global monetary tightening. Long-term U.S. Treasury yields approached 5% amid inflation concerns, while financial markets grapple with waning liquidity conditions.
sections.AI & Economy: Korea's banking sector launched AI-focused investment products including the KB Global Future Growth Industry Fund targeting AI value chains spanning semiconductor infrastructure, physical AI applications, and power infrastructure. Korea Telecom completed the acquisition of Incab America through TFO Networks, securing North American optical cable production capacity to capitalize on AI data center infrastructure demand expansion. The government introduced a National Participation Growth Fund with loss protection guarantees for AI and semiconductor investments, enabling 150 trillion won allocation to high-tech industries. Omidyar Network and other funds emphasized simultaneous investment and social contribution in emerging technology sectors.
sections.Others: Japan's Economy and Industry Minister confirmed additional UAE crude oil supply commitments amid OPEC exit, securing energy supply stability for 40% of Japan's oil imports. Korea's Trade Association participated in SelectUSA to address Korean companies' regulatory challenges with the U.S. government. The government delegated 50 trillion won in expenditure restructuring oversight to private sector ombudsmen and civil society organizations, marking departure from traditional bureaucratic budget controls. Iran dismissed Trump's 'Project Freedom' suspension as failure concealment, continuing geopolitical tensions that ripple through global energy and financial markets.
